conviction_note: Peers that reported after AMAT last spoke (KLA Dec-q guide +13.5% q/q and above consensus, Lam Dec-q guide above consensus with 2027 WFE >$200bn, ASML Q4 guide +25% q/q) point to a Q1 FY27 guide at or above the ~$10.73bn bar (single, undated source), but AMAT sold its last record print with a guide 7% above consensus (-5.12%), Lam fell ~8% on a record beat-and-raise on 2026-10-22, China is set to fall (Lam) with the Affiliates Rule suspension ending inside AMAT's FQ1, and the stock is +22% in five sessions into the print; the call-bid skew (-14.1) argues against the reaction negative, so p_up sits at 48 on an abs move of 8% (implied 7.04%, realised vol 86%), and the near-zero sum of findings agrees with the near-zero scaled number.
bar: FQ4 (Oct) revenue: consensus $10.30bn (Benzinga https://it.benzinga.com/quote/AMAT/earnings-forecasts; Earnings Whispers via Finviz 2026-11-04 https://finviz.com/news/416165/applied-materials-brings-record-ai-demand-into-a-report-the-market-has-stopped-trusting) and $10,299M (Hudson Labs 2026-10-12 https://www.hudson-labs.com/research/applied-materials-q4-2026-earnings-preview-amat-results-preview) against company guide $10.25bn +/- $0.5bn; non-GAAP EPS consensus $4.00-$4.06 against guide $4.02 +/- $0.20, whisper $4.20 (Earnings Whispers). FQ1 FY27 (14-week quarter, no company guide yet, management said sequential growth): revenue consensus $10.73bn, EPS $4.20, from one undated Benzinga page only, so findings that depend on the guide bar are capped small.
positioning_check: Short interest ~13.5M shares, ~1.7% of float, 2.0 days to cover at the 2026-09-30 settlement (down from ~14.1M / 2.4 days on 2026-09-15) per https://curvedtrading.com/stocks/amat/short-interest/ and https://tapeboard.com/stock/AMAT/short-squeeze/ : not crowded, no squeeze mechanism. Skew 25d = -14.1 vol points (calls paid over puts, 'upside paid'), put/call OI 0.65, implied move 7.04%, ATM IV 119%. Earnings Whispers bullish sentiment 19.8% vs 25.1% before the last print (2026-11-04). Tape: -45.9% from the $723 June 30 high, -38.7% Oct 7 to Nov 5, -13.6% on Nov 5 (SOX -12.25%), then +11.4% Nov 9 and +22.45% over five sessions into the seal at $390.92.

findings.finding: Peers that reported after AMAT's 2026-08-13 call guided the December quarter up sharply: KLA guided $4.7bn +/- $0.2bn (+13.5% q/q from $4.14bn) vs ~$4.49bn consensus; Lam guided $8.6bn +/- $0.4bn (+5% q/q) vs ~$8.5bn consensus, said it would have been higher without supply constraints, raised CY2026 WFE to mid-$150bn and gave a preliminary CY2027 WFE of >$200bn; ASML guided Q4 EUR14.2-15.2bn vs Q3 EUR11.7bn and said 2027-28 supply falls short of demand. That points to AMAT's FQ1 FY27 (14-week) guide landing at or above the ~$10.73bn consensus (+4.7% over the FQ4 bar) and to a 2027 view of 'another strong year' consistent with ~30% WFE growth.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: 2026-08-13: FQ4 guide of $10.25bn vs $9.55bn consensus (+7%) and EPS $4.02 vs $3.71, and the stock fell -5.12% (siliconangle: Stifel said Lam and KLA had already set the bar). 2026-02-12 +8.08% is the only large up reaction in 7 prints. The guide line has been sold more often than bought.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: these guides were public by 2026-10-28, but the stock then fell 13.6% on 2026-11-05 on fears of an AI capex slowdown (not a drop in current orders), so the market is now discounting 2027 below what the peers' WFE >$200bn implies. If it were fully priced, AMAT would not be 46% off its high at ~8x trailing sales with bullish sentiment at 19.8%; AMAT's own Oct 13 investor day deferred any quarterly or 2027 revenue number to this call, so this is the first company-level statement since the peers spoke.
findings.independence: Lam guide and 2027 WFE from a different document: https://www.marketbeat.com/articles/lam-researchs-earnings-beat-wasnt-the-real-storyits-2027-outlook-was/ (2026-10-22); ASML: https://investinglive.com/stocks/asml-says-2027-and-2028-supply-will-fall-short-of-demand-as-q3-sales-hit-a-record/ (2026-10-14). These three are combined here as one finding (one peer read-through).

findings.finding: China is likely to fall in AMAT's guide quarter: Lam said China's share (35% in the Sept quarter, up from 26%) will drop significantly in the December quarter on lower domestic-customer revenue, and the BIS Affiliates Rule suspension was extended on 2026-11-05 only to 2027-01-10, a date inside AMAT's FQ1 FY27; AMAT said in August that China (28% of revenue, $2.506bn in FQ3) would grow in both 2026 and 2027, and in 2025 it sized the Affiliates Rule at ~$600m of annual revenue. Softer China language or a haircut in the FQ1 guide is the risk; net of the rest of the company, DRAM (26% of systems, +52% y/y) and leading edge would need to absorb it.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: China/export lines have moved the stock before: the 2025 Affiliates Rule warning of a ~$600m FY26 hit hit the stock (TipRanks, 2025-10); 2025-08-14 -14.07% came with a weak China/outlook. Lam fell ~8% premarket on 2026-10-22 with this China comment in its release.
findings.why_not_priced: The extension was read as good news (the rule did not snap back on Nov 10), while the short duration to Jan 10 sits inside AMAT's guided quarter; no AMAT preview found (Hudson Labs, Earnings Whispers) quantifies China for FQ1. If priced, previews would carry a China haircut to the $10.73bn FQ1 bar; they do not mention one.
findings.independence: Lam's China guidance from a separate document: https://www.marketbeat.com/articles/lam-researchs-earnings-beat-wasnt-the-real-storyits-2027-outlook-was/ (2026-10-22). AMAT's own prior China statements: https://www.webull.com/news/15400606166574080 (2026-08-14) and https://finviz.com/news/416165/applied-materials-brings-record-ai-demand-into-a-report-the-market-has-stopped-trusting (2026-11-04).

findings.finding: This name and its group sell good prints: AMAT fell on 5 of its last 7 prints (median |move| 5.25%), including -5.12% after a record FQ3 with a guide 7% above consensus; Lam fell ~8% premarket on 2026-10-22 after a record quarter and an above-consensus guide; AMAT fell ~7% on its 2026-10-13 investor day on 2030 targets with no revenue target. The stock goes into this print +22.45% over five sessions after the Nov 5 crash, so part of a relief rally is already in the price.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Baseline: -5.12, -0.89, +8.08, +1.25, -14.07, -5.25, -8.18 (2 of 7 up). August 2026: beat and big guide raise sold.
findings.why_not_priced: The option market leans the other way (25d skew -14.1, calls bid), so the implied distribution does not carry a sell-the-news lean; the five-day +22% move into the print raises the bar in the same way the peer guides did in August. Sized down because it runs against a strong call skew and short interest is low (1.7% of float), so this is not a squeeze argument either way.

findings.finding: Sentiment and valuation were reset before the print: Earnings Whispers bullish sentiment fell to 19.8% from 25.1% before the last report; shares were -23.5% since the last report and below the ~$444 200-day average as of 2026-11-04, and fell a further 13.6% on 2026-11-05 to $319.25 (-38.7% from Oct 7) on group-wide selling with no company news; P/S fell to ~8.2x.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: 2026-02-12 +8.08% followed a period of weak sentiment; otherwise no clean analogue in the baseline.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly unwound already by the +22% five-session rebound to $390.92; the low bullish-sentiment reading was taken before that rebound. If the reset were fully reversed, the stock would be back near the $444 200-day line.

findings.finding: TSMC (AMAT's largest foundry customer) said on 2026-10-15/17 it is 'being prudent in our business planning going into 2027', held 2026 capex at $60-64bn, and said 2026-2028 capex will be 'significantly higher than in the previous three years'; Microsoft lowered CY2026 capex to ~$170bn on third-party capacity delays and Meta gave no 2027 budget. This is the customer-side backdrop to the AI-capex fear that drove the Nov 5 crash, and it frames AMAT's 2027 commentary.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No baseline print turned on TSMC commentary directly; 2025-08-14 -14.07% came with caution on visibility.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: the fear is in the 46% drawdown. Kept small and filed because AMAT's 2027 framing will be read against it, and TSMC's caution refers to consumer segments rather than leading-edge capex.
findings.independence: Proxy (customer commentary, not confirmed by AMAT). Hyperscaler capex tracker: https://walnutinvest.com/stats/ai-capex-statistics

findings.finding: Memory capex is rising into 2027: SK hynix raised 2026 capex ~50% to at least KRW45tn and said on 2026-10-29 that longer equipment lead times are constraining expansion, with >50% of 2027-28 capacity under contract; Samsung's 2026 capex reported at KRW84.4tn with HBM sold out through 2027. DRAM was 26% of AMAT systems revenue (+52% y/y) in FQ3; Lam's memory was 46% of systems, +120% y/y.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: DRAM strength was cited on the Aug 2026 print, which was sold.
findings.why_not_priced: Public and partly embedded in the peer guides (finding 1); filed separately only because it is the memory customers themselves, not equipment peers, and the memory/equipment names were the hardest hit on Nov 5 (Micron -17.5%, Lam -16.4%).
findings.independence: Proxy (customer capex). Samsung: https://book.st-hakky.com/en/news/samsung-ai-chip-2027-sold-out-increases-investment ; overlaps in substance with the Lam memory figure in finding 1.

findings.finding: AMAT's 2026-10-13 investor day gave 2030 margin targets (~54% GM, ~40% OM), >2pt WFE share gain, services >$12bn and 80-100% FCF return, but no total revenue target, no WFE growth number and no orders/backlog, deferring quarterly guidance to this call; the stock fell 6.7-7.2% that day. This call is the first company-level 2027 number since then, which raises the size of the move rather than setting its sign.
findings.why_not_priced: Sign is not determinable; filed as a magnitude item (it moves abs_move_pct, not the sum).

findings.finding: AMAT 8-K of 2026-10-26: Applied will raise its BE Semiconductor (Besi) stake from ~9% to ~20% via an accelerated purchase, pending US antitrust clearance, with no intent to go beyond ~20% or seek a board seat. The money buys hybrid-bonding/advanced-packaging exposure (packaging +70% in CY2026), which supports a ramp, but it is cash that would otherwise go to buybacks this quarter.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No baseline print turned on capital deployment.
findings.why_not_priced: Public since Oct 26; the money funds a visible packaging ramp, so it is signed zero after asking what it buys. Watch only whether the FQ4 buyback pace slowed.

findings.finding: FQ1 FY27 EPS headwinds already flagged by management: a 14-week quarter with higher opex, and a tax rate rising to ~13% in 2027 from ~11%, against an FQ1 EPS consensus of $4.20 (single source); gross margin guided roughly flat at ~50.4% in FQ4 as hiring and capacity costs absorb leverage.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Margin/EPS guide was not the cited driver of recent reactions.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced: management said it, so it sits inside what the company already guided; sized near zero.

Nvidia's earnings (reported as expected around 2026-11-17, date unconfirmed) are the next AI-capex read for the group, after the exit window.

baseline_tension: The fundamentals read (peer guides, memory capex) is positive and agrees with the call-bid skew, while the reaction function (5 of 7 prints down, last guide raise sold, +22% into the print) cuts against it, so the two offset and p_up sits just under 50.
lessons_applied: Lesson 6 (bar): the FQ1 FY27 consensus ($10.73bn / $4.20) has a single undated source, so the peer-guide finding was capped from +1.5 to +1.2; the FQ4 bar has two agreeing sources plus the company guide.
Lesson 7 (skew): the sell-the-news positioning finding runs against a -14.1 call-bid skew and short interest is only 1.7% of float, so it was shrunk from -1.5 to -1.0; p_up moved from 47 to 48.
Lesson 9 (segment net of the rest): the China finding was trimmed from -1.0 to -0.8 because DRAM and leading edge (~72% of revenue) would absorb part of a China dip.
Lesson 6 (inside the guide): the tax/14-week opex EPS finding was already flagged by management, so it went from -0.3 to -0.1.
Lesson 1 (reaction function) was applied once, via the separate positioning finding, and not again to the peer-guide finding, so the same concern is not counted twice.
